recentItems.description:
Reading, maths and science scores in PISA, the world’s biggest international test of 15-year-olds, are falling. The downward trend started around 2012 and seems to be accelerating, particularly in reading. Here we explore some of the theories about what’s causing the decline.

recentItems.title: UK expected to announce sanctions on Israeli settlements in occupied West Bank | BBC News
recentItems.description:
The UK is expected to announce sanctions on goods and services from Israeli settlements in the illegally occupied West Bank.
 
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is due to announce the move in the House of Commons on Tuesday afternoon, having previously said the UK-Israel relationship will be “reset”.
 
The settlements are illegal under international law and the UK's move comes as Israel opens tenders for 1,200 new homes in the occupied territory.
 
US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee said the US opposes the UK imposing sanctions, and he told the BBC that US states could retaliate against the UK.

recentItems.title: Iran warns of 'heavier response' after trading strikes with US in Strait of Hormuz | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Iran's top negotiator warns of "a faster, heavier, and more painful response" to US attacks, after the sides traded strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. 
 
It comes as Iran's security chief says Tehran will announce a prohibited zone outside the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days, saying any ship entering the area will be added to a sanctions list.

Can The Chancellor John Healey's Positive Vibes Limit UK Tax Rises? | BBC Newscast
recentItems.description:
Today, John Healey delivered his first major speech as chancellor, aiming to boost confidence in the economy with a positive message.

The chancellor set out his intentions for growth, investment and more jobs. But midway through, Jaguar Land Rover announced they would be making thousands of job cuts after struggling with competition from China and falling behind in the electric vehicle race.

Economics editor Faisal Islam and business editor Simon Jack explain what it means for the country, and they chat through Healey’s new ‘Make Great Britain Growth Britain Again”

And we've had a weekend of anti-migration protests. One involved men in balaclavas in Dover and one with a crowd trying to block the migrant coaches in Portsmouth. UK correspondent Daniel Sandford explains.

Was Saudi Arabia involved in 9/11? | The Global Story
recentItems.description:
Twenty-five years on from the deadliest terror attack in history, thousands of grieving families are still fighting for answers.

In early 2000, two young Saudis arrived in San Diego. They had never been to America, spoke almost no English, and had no idea how to open a bank account or rent a flat. Within weeks they had done all of it. Twenty months later they hijacked a plane and crashed it into the Pentagon.

The BBC’s Jane McMullen has been investigating a man who helped two of the hijackers – and has revealed a story that the US and Saudi governments have fought to keep secret.

recentItems.title: What is the AfD and what could their victory mean for Germany and Europe? | BBC News
recentItems.description:
"Seismic", "a socio-political earthquake", "a watershed moment for Germany".
 
This was how political analysts and many media outlets described the stunning victory of the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in local elections in Germany on Sunday. Is that an exaggeration?
 
Saxony-Anhalt is one of the smallest of massive Germany's 16 regions. It boasts a mere 1.7 million out of 59 million eligible voters nationwide.
 
How significant can its political sentiments be, especially since the AfD narrowly failed to win an outright majority?
 
The answer: Very significant.

recentItems.title: German Chancellor Merz ‘shocked’ by far-right AfD win and other news stories | Global News Podcast
recentItems.description:
Chancellor Friedrich Merz says Germany is facing a tectonic shift in party politics, following the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD)'s victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. Mr Merz said the result had shaken his conservative CDU to its core, signalling the need for a major reckoning. The anti-immigration AfD has proposed banning LGBTQ rainbow flags in schools and teaching the children of refugees in segregated classes.
